title: What's in the Kitchen
summary: A picture guide to the knives, boards, pots and pans, utensils, measuring tools, small appliances, bakeware, thermometers and containers in a family kitchen: what each one is, what it is for, and how to clean and care for it.

groups.intro: A sharp knife is a safer knife: it goes where you aim it and needs less push. Most home cooks need only three.

tools.name: Chef's knife
tools.what: An 8-inch knife with a wide blade that curves up to a point.
tools.for: Chopping, slicing and mincing almost anything: onions, carrots, herbs, meat.
tools.care: Wash by hand, dry right away, and store it in a block, on a magnetic strip or in a sheath.
tools.svg: <path class="m" d="M76 27 L76 49 Q36 52 8 45 Q38 31 76 27 Z"/><rect class="d" x="76" y="30" width="6" height="18" rx="2"/><rect class="d" x="82" y="32" width="32" height="13" rx="5"/><circle class="m" cx="90" cy="38.5" r="1.8"/><circle class="m" cx="98" cy="38.5" r="1.8"/><circle class="m" cx="106" cy="38.5" r="1.8"/>

tools.name: Paring knife
tools.what: A small knife with a 3- to 4-inch blade.
tools.for: Small jobs held in the hand or on the board: hulling strawberries, trimming, peeling.
tools.care: Same as the chef’s knife: hand-wash, dry, and keep it out of a loose drawer.
tools.svg: <path class="m" d="M64 34 L64 46 Q40 48 22 43 Q40 36 64 34 Z"/><rect class="g" x="64" y="35" width="32" height="10" rx="4"/><circle class="m" cx="74" cy="40" r="1.8"/><circle class="m" cx="86" cy="40" r="1.8"/>

tools.name: Serrated (bread) knife
tools.what: A long knife with a toothed edge, like a saw.
tools.for: Bread, tomatoes and anything with a crust or a slippery skin. Saw gently instead of pressing.
tools.care: Hand-wash and dry. Serrated edges need a special sharpener, so many families have them sharpened by a pro.

tools.name: Kitchen shears
tools.what: Strong scissors for food.
tools.for: Snipping herbs and green onions, cutting up chicken, opening packages.
tools.care: Many come apart at the hinge for washing. Dry well so the pivot does not rust.

tools.name: Honing steel
tools.what: A rod with a handle and a guard.
tools.for: Honing: it pushes a knife’s bent edge back into line. It does not grind away metal, so it does not sharpen. Many cooks hone before each use.
tools.care: Wipe clean. Hold the knife at the same angle each stroke.
tools.svg: <rect class="m" x="8" y="37" width="68" height="6" rx="3"/><path class="l" d="M16 37v6M24 37v6M32 37v6M40 37v6M48 37v6M56 37v6M64 37v6"/><rect class="m2" x="76" y="29" width="5" height="22" rx="2"/><rect class="d" x="81" y="34" width="32" height="12" rx="5"/><circle class="h" cx="108" cy="40" r="2"/>

tools.name: Sharpening stone
tools.what: A whetstone (or a pull-through or electric sharpener).
tools.for: Sharpening: it grinds off a little metal to make a new edge. Needed far less often than honing, about once a month for a busy kitchen knife.
tools.care: Follow the stone’s directions for water or oil. Let it dry before you put it away.

groups.intro: Keep at least two: one for raw meat, poultry and seafood, and one for produce and foods that won’t be cooked.

tools.name: Wooden cutting board
tools.what: A board of hardwood such as maple.
tools.for: Everyday chopping. Wood is easy on knife edges.
tools.care: Wash with hot, soapy water, rinse and dry upright. Don’t soak it. Rub with food-safe mineral oil about once a month.

tools.name: Plastic cutting board
tools.what: A board of plastic, often with a groove to catch juice.
tools.for: A good choice for raw meat, poultry and seafood, since it can be scrubbed and sanitized thoroughly.
tools.care: Wash with hot, soapy water; many can go in the dishwasher. Replace it when deep grooves won’t come clean.
tools.svg: <rect class="b" x="8" y="22" width="104" height="40" rx="6"/><rect class="o l" x="15" y="28" width="90" height="28" rx="5"/><rect class="g n" x="94" y="24" width="14" height="4" rx="2"/>

groups.intro: Each metal heats and cleans a little differently. The care guide has the details.

tools.name: Cast iron skillet
tools.what: A heavy, one-piece iron pan with a dark, seasoned surface.
tools.for: Searing, frying, cornbread, and anything that likes steady, even heat. It goes from stove to oven.
tools.care: Wash (a little soap is fine), dry completely, rub with a thin coat of oil. No soaking, no dishwasher.

tools.name: Carbon steel pan
tools.what: A lighter, thinner cousin of cast iron with a long handle.
tools.for: Quick searing, eggs, vegetables and fish. It heats up and cools down faster than cast iron.
tools.care: Same care as cast iron: wash in warm water, dry, oil.
tools.svg: <ellipse class="d" cx="44" cy="48" rx="36" ry="17"/><ellipse class="d2" cx="44" cy="45" rx="27" ry="10"/><polygon class="d" points="78,42 116,26 118,31 80,50"/><circle class="m" cx="88" cy="42.5" r="1.6"/><circle class="m" cx="96" cy="39.2" r="1.6"/>

tools.name: Stainless steel skillet
tools.what: A shiny pan, often with an aluminum or copper core for even heat.
tools.for: Browning, pan sauces and everyday cooking. It won’t react with tomatoes or wine.
tools.care: Preheat on low to medium. Soak stuck food in warm, soapy water; a nonabrasive cleanser handles the rest.
tools.svg: <ellipse class="m" cx="44" cy="48" rx="36" ry="17"/><ellipse class="m2" cx="44" cy="45" rx="28" ry="11"/><path class="m" d="M78 43 L114 31 Q119 31 118 36 L80 50 Z"/><circle class="h" cx="113" cy="34" r="1.8"/>

tools.name: Nonstick skillet
tools.what: A pan with a slick coating inside.
tools.for: Eggs, pancakes and delicate fish that stick elsewhere.
tools.care: Low to medium heat. Wood, silicone or nylon tools only. Wash by hand with a soft sponge.
tools.svg: <ellipse class="g" cx="44" cy="48" rx="36" ry="17"/><ellipse class="d" cx="44" cy="45" rx="28" ry="11"/><path class="d" d="M78 43 L112 32 Q118 31 118 36 L82 51 Z"/><rect class="y n" x="84" y="42" width="5" height="4" rx="1" transform="rotate(-18 86 44)"/>

tools.name: Saucepan
tools.what: A deep pan with straight sides and one long handle.
tools.for: Rice, oatmeal, sauces, boiling eggs, heating soup.
tools.care: Depends on the metal; most are stainless. Wash in warm, soapy water and dry.

tools.name: Stockpot
tools.what: A tall, wide pot with two loop handles and a lid.
tools.for: Pasta, soups, stock and big batches.
tools.care: Wash in warm, soapy water. Use both hands to lift a full pot.

tools.name: Enameled cast iron
tools.what: Cast iron coated in glassy enamel, often in a bright color.
tools.for: Long simmers, stews, chili and tomato sauces: the enamel handles acidic food. No seasoning needed.
tools.care: Don’t heat it empty. Use wood, silicone or nylon tools. Hand-washing keeps the finish best.

tools.name: Dutch oven
tools.what: A heavy pot with a tight lid, in bare or enameled cast iron. Camp versions have legs and a wire handle.
tools.for: Braising, pot roast, soups and bread, on the stove or in the oven.
tools.care: Bare cast iron gets cast iron care; enameled gets enamel care.

tools.name: Sheet pan
tools.what: A flat metal pan with a low rim, also called a rimmed baking sheet.
tools.for: Roasting vegetables, sheet-pan dinners, cookies.
tools.care: Soak stuck bits in warm, soapy water. Lining it with foil or parchment saves scrubbing.

groups.intro: The hand tools you reach for every day.

tools.name: Wooden spoon
tools.what: A spoon carved from hardwood.
tools.for: Stirring sauces, soups and batters. Safe on every pan.
tools.care: Wash by hand and dry. Rub with food-safe mineral oil when it looks dry.
tools.svg: <ellipse class="w" cx="24" cy="40" rx="17" ry="11"/><ellipse class="w2" cx="24" cy="40" rx="11" ry="6"/><rect class="w" x="40" y="37" width="74" height="6" rx="3"/>

tools.name: Spatula (turner)
tools.what: A flat, wide blade on a handle, often with slots.
tools.for: Flipping pancakes, burgers and eggs; lifting cookies.
tools.care: Use a nylon or silicone turner on nonstick pans.
tools.svg: <rect class="d" x="6" y="26" width="38" height="28" rx="5"/><path class="h" d="M14 32h22M14 40h22M14 48h22" style="stroke:var(--k-bg);stroke-width:3"/><rect class="d" x="44" y="37" width="20" height="6" rx="2"/><rect class="w" x="64" y="35" width="50" height="10" rx="5"/>

tools.name: Rubber or silicone spatula
tools.what: A soft, flexible blade.
tools.for: Scraping every bit out of a bowl, folding batter, stirring eggs.
tools.care: Dishwasher safe in most cases.

tools.name: Whisk
tools.what: Loops of wire joined at a handle.
tools.for: Beating eggs, mixing batter smooth, whipping cream.
tools.care: Rinse right away so batter doesn’t dry between the wires.

tools.name: Tongs
tools.what: Two spring-loaded arms that pinch.
tools.for: Turning meat and vegetables, serving salad and pasta.
tools.care: Use separate tongs (or wash them) after touching raw meat.

tools.name: Ladle
tools.what: A deep cup on a long handle.
tools.for: Serving soup, stew and chili.
tools.care: Dishwasher safe in most cases.

tools.name: Slotted spoon
tools.what: A big spoon with slots or holes.
tools.for: Lifting food out of water or sauce and leaving the liquid behind.
tools.care: Dishwasher safe in most cases.
tools.svg: <ellipse class="m" cx="26" cy="40" rx="18" ry="12"/><path class="l" d="M16 36h20M14 40h24M16 44h20" style="stroke:var(--k-bg);stroke-width:2.6"/><rect class="m" x="42" y="37" width="72" height="6" rx="3"/>

tools.name: Vegetable peeler
tools.what: A handle with a sharp, slotted blade.
tools.for: Peeling carrots, potatoes, apples and cucumbers. Peel away from your hand.
tools.care: The blade is sharp; wash it carefully.
tools.svg: <rect class="g" x="54" y="40" width="12" height="34" rx="6"/><path class="m" d="M56 42 L40 18 L44 16 L60 38 L76 16 L80 18 L64 42 Z"/><rect class="m2" x="38" y="12" width="44" height="7" rx="2"/><path class="l" d="M44 15.5h32"/>

tools.name: Can opener
tools.what: A hand tool with a cutting wheel and a turning key.
tools.for: Opening cans.
tools.care: Wash the cutting wheel after each use; it touches the food.
tools.svg: <polygon class="g" points="44,37 114,27 116,33 48,44"/><polygon class="g" points="44,45 114,55 116,49 48,38"/><rect class="m" x="6" y="34" width="30" height="14" rx="7"/><circle class="m" cx="40" cy="41" r="11"/><circle class="m2" cx="40" cy="41" r="4"/><path class="l" d="M40 30v-3M40 52v3M29 41h-2"/>

tools.name: Colander
tools.what: A bowl full of holes, with feet or handles.
tools.for: Draining pasta, rinsing fruit and vegetables.
tools.care: Rinse right away; starch is easier to clean before it dries.
tools.svg: <path class="m" d="M16 30 L104 30 Q102 62 60 66 Q18 62 16 30 Z"/><ellipse class="m2" cx="60" cy="30" rx="44" ry="7"/><path class="o" d="M16 32 Q4 32 6 40 Q8 44 18 42M104 32 Q116 32 114 40 Q112 44 102 42"/><path class="l" d="M44 66 L40 74 L80 74 L76 66"/><circle class="h n" cx="34" cy="42" r="2"/><circle class="h n" cx="46" cy="44" r="2"/><circle class="h n" cx="58" cy="45" r="2"/><circle class="h n" cx="70" cy="44" r="2"/><circle class="h n" cx="82" cy="42" r="2"/><circle class="h n" cx="40" cy="52" r="2"/><circle class="h n" cx="52" cy="54" r="2"/><circle class="h n" cx="64" cy="54" r="2"/><circle class="h n" cx="76" cy="52" r="2"/><circle class="h n" cx="58" cy="61" r="2"/><circle class="h n" cx="48" cy="61" r="2"/><circle class="h n" cx="68" cy="61" r="2"/>

tools.name: Box grater
tools.what: A metal box with a different cutting face on each side.
tools.for: Grating cheese, carrots, zucchini and lemon zest.
tools.care: Scrub with a brush from the inside out. Keep fingers well away from the blades.

tools.name: Potato masher
tools.what: A handle with a wavy wire or a holed plate at the end.
tools.for: Mashing potatoes, beans and bananas.
tools.care: Dishwasher safe in most cases.

groups.intro: Baking needs careful measuring; soups and stir-fries forgive a little. Dry and liquid cups hold the same amount but are made to be used differently.

tools.name: Dry measuring cups
tools.what: Nested cups: 1, ½, ⅓ and ¼ cup.
tools.for: Flour, sugar, oats, rice. Spoon flour in and level the top with a straight edge.
tools.care: Dry completely before stacking.
tools.svg: <path class="m" d="M4 42 L38 42 L35 72 L7 72 Z"/><rect class="m" x="36" y="42" width="12" height="4" rx="2"/><text class="t" x="21.0" y="61.0" text-anchor="middle">1</text><path class="m" d="M46 48 L74 48 L71 72 L49 72 Z"/><rect class="m" x="72" y="48" width="12" height="4" rx="2"/><text class="t" x="60.0" y="64.0" text-anchor="middle">½</text><path class="m" d="M82 54 L104 54 L101 72 L85 72 Z"/><rect class="m" x="102" y="54" width="12" height="4" rx="2"/><text class="t" x="93.0" y="67.0" text-anchor="middle">⅓</text>

tools.name: Liquid measuring cup
tools.what: A clear cup with a spout and lines on the side.
tools.for: Water, milk, broth and oil. Set it on the counter and read the line at eye level.
tools.care: Glass ones can go in the dishwasher.
tools.svg: <path class="s" d="M30 20 L84 20 L80 72 L34 72 Z"/><path class="s" d="M30 20 L20 16 L31 30"/><path class="o" d="M83 28 Q104 30 102 46 Q100 62 80 62" style="stroke-width:4"/><path class="gl" d="M34 34h14M35 46h14M36 58h14"/><text class="t" x="54" y="37">1 c</text><text class="t" x="55" y="49">¾</text><text class="t" x="56" y="61">½</text>

tools.name: Measuring spoons
tools.what: A set of spoons: 1 tablespoon (T), 1 teaspoon (t), ½ and ¼ teaspoon.
tools.for: Baking powder, salt, spices, vanilla. 3 teaspoons make 1 tablespoon.
tools.care: Keep them on their ring so none go missing.
tools.svg: <ellipse class="m" cx="18" cy="30" rx="11" ry="8.8"/><rect class="m" x="16" y="37.7" width="4" height="27" rx="2"/><ellipse class="m" cx="46" cy="30" rx="9" ry="7.2"/><rect class="m" x="44" y="36.3" width="4" height="29" rx="2"/><ellipse class="m" cx="70" cy="30" rx="7" ry="5.6000000000000005"/><rect class="m" x="68" y="34.9" width="4" height="31" rx="2"/><ellipse class="m" cx="90" cy="30" rx="5.5" ry="4.4"/><rect class="m" x="88" y="33.85" width="4" height="32.5" rx="2"/><text class="t" x="18" y="34" text-anchor="middle">T</text><text class="t" x="46" y="34" text-anchor="middle">t</text>

tools.name: Kitchen scale
tools.what: A flat digital scale that weighs in grams and ounces.
tools.for: The most exact way to measure, especially flour. The “tare” button sets the bowl to zero.
tools.care: Wipe with a damp cloth; never put it in water.

groups.intro: Read the manual that came with each one: it has the cleaning steps and the limits for that model.

tools.name: Slow cooker
tools.what: A heavy crock that sits in a heating base, with a lid.
tools.for: Pot roast, pulled pork, chili and soups that cook gently for hours.
tools.care: Thaw meat and poultry before it goes in, and keep the lid on. The crock washes in warm, soapy water; never put the base in water.

tools.name: Electric pressure cooker
tools.what: A pot that locks shut and cooks under steam pressure; many also slow cook.
tools.for: Beans, stews, rice and tough cuts of meat, much faster than a stove.
tools.care: Wash the inner pot, lid, gasket and steam valve as the manual says; a clogged valve or worn gasket needs attention before you cook.
tools.svg: <rect class="b" x="26" y="30" width="68" height="44" rx="12"/><path class="d" d="M22 34 Q60 10 98 34 Z"/><rect class="m" x="66" y="16" width="10" height="7" rx="2"/><rect class="d" x="44" y="46" width="32" height="16" rx="3"/><text class="t tl" x="60" y="57.5" text-anchor="middle">0:30</text><rect class="d" x="18" y="40" width="8" height="12" rx="2"/><rect class="d" x="94" y="40" width="8" height="12" rx="2"/>

tools.name: Blender
tools.what: A tall jar with blades in the bottom, on a motor base.
tools.for: Smoothies, soups, sauces.
tools.care: Fill it partway with warm water and a drop of dish soap, blend, rinse. Unplug before reaching near the blades.
tools.svg: <polygon class="s" points="40,60 80,60 88,12 32,12"/><rect class="d" x="30" y="6" width="60" height="8" rx="3"/><path class="o" d="M85 20 Q102 22 100 36 Q98 50 82 50" style="stroke-width:4"/><path class="l" d="M50 54 L60 50 L70 54M60 50 L60 58"/><path class="d" d="M36 60 L84 60 L88 76 L32 76 Z"/><circle class="m n" cx="50" cy="68" r="2.5"/><circle class="m n" cx="60" cy="68" r="2.5"/><circle class="m n" cx="70" cy="68" r="2.5"/>

tools.name: Stand mixer
tools.what: A motor head that turns a beater in a bowl.
tools.for: Cake batter, cookie dough, whipped cream, bread dough.
tools.care: Wash the bowl and attachments; wipe the body with a damp cloth.

tools.name: Toaster oven
tools.what: A small countertop oven.
tools.for: Toast, reheating, and baking small batches without heating the big oven.
tools.care: Unplug and let it cool, then empty the crumb tray. Crumbs can burn.

tools.name: Air fryer
tools.what: A small countertop convection oven with a pull-out basket.
tools.for: Crisping vegetables, fries, chicken and leftovers with little oil.
tools.care: Unplug and cool, then wash the basket in warm, soapy water.
tools.svg: <rect class="d" x="30" y="8" width="60" height="68" rx="16"/><circle class="m" cx="60" cy="23" r="6"/><path class="l" d="M60 23 L63 19"/><rect class="b" x="34" y="38" width="52" height="30" rx="7"/><rect class="d" x="51" y="48" width="18" height="8" rx="3"/>

tools.name: Microwave oven
tools.what: A box that heats food with microwaves.
tools.for: Reheating, steaming vegetables, melting butter. Cover food, stir halfway, and let it stand before checking the temperature.
tools.care: Wipe up spills as they happen. No metal or foil inside.

groups.intro: Metal pans brown faster; glass and ceramic heat slower and hold heat longer.

tools.name: Loaf pan
tools.what: A deep rectangle, about 9 by 5 inches.
tools.for: Bread, banana bread, meatloaf.
tools.care: Grease or line with parchment so loaves come out clean.

tools.name: Muffin tin
tools.what: A pan with 6 or 12 cups.
tools.for: Muffins, cupcakes, egg muffin cups.
tools.care: Paper liners save scrubbing.
tools.svg: <polygon class="m" points="8,58 26,24 112,24 94,58"/><ellipse class="m2" cx="36" cy="32" rx="9" ry="5"/><ellipse class="m2" cx="60" cy="32" rx="9" ry="5"/><ellipse class="m2" cx="84" cy="32" rx="9" ry="5"/><ellipse class="m2" cx="29" cy="46" rx="9" ry="5"/><ellipse class="m2" cx="55" cy="46" rx="9" ry="5"/><ellipse class="m2" cx="80" cy="46" rx="9" ry="5"/><polygon class="m" points="8,58 94,58 94,63 8,63"/>

tools.name: Baking dish (9 by 13)
tools.what: A deep glass or ceramic dish.
tools.for: Lasagna, baked ziti, casseroles, brownies.
tools.care: Don’t move a hot glass dish to a cold, wet surface; sudden temperature changes can crack it.
tools.svg: <polygon class="s" points="12,56 30,26 108,26 90,56"/><polygon class="s" points="20,52 34,30 100,30 86,52"/><polygon class="s" points="12,56 90,56 88,64 14,64"/><rect class="s" x="2" y="55" width="12" height="6" rx="3"/><rect class="s" x="88" y="55" width="12" height="6" rx="3"/>

tools.name: Round cake pan
tools.what: A shallow round pan, 8 or 9 inches.
tools.for: Layer cakes, cornbread.
tools.care: Grease and flour it, or line the bottom with a circle of parchment.
tools.svg: <path class="m" d="M14 34 L14 50 A46 14 0 0 0 106 50 L106 34"/><ellipse class="m2" cx="60" cy="34" rx="46" ry="14"/><ellipse class="o l" cx="60" cy="36" rx="38" ry="10"/>

tools.name: Pie plate
tools.what: A shallow dish with sloped sides.
tools.for: Pies, quiche.
tools.care: Soak baked-on filling in warm, soapy water.

tools.name: Cooling rack
tools.what: A wire grid on little feet.
tools.for: Cooling cookies and bread so the bottoms don’t get soggy; also for oven-crisping.
tools.care: Soak, then scrub with a brush.

tools.name: Rolling pin
tools.what: A smooth wooden or marble roller.
tools.for: Rolling out pie crust, cookies and pizza dough.
tools.care: Scrape off dough, wipe with a damp cloth and dry. Don’t soak wood.
tools.svg: <rect class="w" x="26" y="30" width="68" height="20" rx="10"/><rect class="w" x="6" y="36" width="16" height="8" rx="4"/><rect class="w" x="98" y="36" width="16" height="8" rx="4"/><path class="o" d="M22 40 L26 40M94 40 L98 40"/>

groups.intro: Color isn’t a reliable sign that food is done. A thermometer is the only sure way.

tools.name: Instant-read thermometer
tools.what: A digital thermometer with a thin probe; reads in a few seconds.
tools.for: Checking meat, poultry, fish, casseroles and leftovers. Put the tip in the thickest part, away from bone.
tools.care: Wash the probe with hot, soapy water after each use, especially after raw meat.
tools.svg: <path class="m" d="M8 40 L66 37 L66 43 Z"/><rect class="g" x="66" y="28" width="46" height="24" rx="9"/><rect class="d" x="72" y="33" width="26" height="14" rx="2"/><text class="t tl" x="85" y="43.5" text-anchor="middle">165°</text><circle class="y n" cx="105" cy="40" r="3"/>

tools.name: Dial thermometer
tools.what: A round dial on a metal stem; some can stay in a roast in the oven.
tools.for: Roasts and thick foods. Push the stem in up to the dimple mark.
tools.care: Check it in ice water now and then: it should read 32°F. Many dials have a nut to adjust.
tools.svg: <rect class="m" x="8" y="38" width="72" height="4" rx="2"/><circle class="b" cx="94" cy="40" r="20"/><circle class="o l" cx="94" cy="40" r="15"/><path class="o" d="M94 40 L104 32"/><circle class="d n" cx="94" cy="40" r="2.5"/><path class="l" d="M94 27v3M107 40h-3M81 40h3M94 53v-3"/>

tools.name: Fridge and freezer thermometer
tools.what: A small dial or bulb thermometer that hangs or stands on a shelf.
tools.for: Making sure the fridge is at 40°F or below and the freezer at 0°F or below. The built-in dial alone can’t tell you.
tools.care: Leave it in place and glance at it every week.
tools.svg: <path class="o" d="M60 6 L60 14"/><circle class="o" cx="60" cy="5" r="3"/><rect class="b" x="38" y="14" width="44" height="60" rx="8"/><circle class="o l" cx="60" cy="38" r="14"/><path class="o" d="M60 38 L54 28"/><circle class="d n" cx="60" cy="38" r="2.2"/><text class="t" x="60" y="66" text-anchor="middle">40°F</text>

groups.intro: Shallow containers cool food fastest. Label everything with what it is and the date.

tools.name: Glass container with lid
tools.what: Glass with a snap-on lid.
tools.for: Leftovers and meal prep; reheat in the glass (lid off or vented).
tools.care: Dishwasher safe in most cases. Let hot glass cool before it goes in the freezer.
tools.svg: <rect class="s" x="14" y="36" width="92" height="32" rx="6"/><rect class="g" x="10" y="28" width="100" height="10" rx="4"/><rect class="g" x="22" y="36" width="10" height="7" rx="2"/><rect class="g" x="88" y="36" width="10" height="7" rx="2"/>

tools.name: Plastic deli container
tools.what: A round, stackable container, often in pint and quart sizes.
tools.for: Soups, sauces, cooked grains, and freezing portions.
tools.care: Leave a little room at the top for food to expand as it freezes.
tools.svg: <polygon class="s" points="34,30 86,30 80,72 40,72"/><ellipse class="b" cx="60" cy="28" rx="30" ry="6"/><path class="l" d="M38 40 L82 40"/><text class="t" x="60" y="60" text-anchor="middle">1 qt</text>

tools.name: Freezer bag
tools.what: A thick, zip-top plastic bag.
tools.for: Freezing soup flat, marinating, storing chopped vegetables.
tools.care: Press out the air and write the name and date on it before filling.
tools.svg: <rect class="s" x="22" y="12" width="76" height="62" rx="4"/><rect class="g" x="22" y="12" width="76" height="8" rx="2"/><rect class="b" x="32" y="28" width="56" height="18" rx="2"/><text class="t" x="60" y="40" text-anchor="middle">soup 10/30</text>

tools.name: Glass jar
tools.what: A canning jar with a lid and band.
tools.for: Pantry staples like rice and beans, overnight oats, dressings.
tools.care: Dishwasher safe. Jars kept in the pantry with tight lids help keep pests out.
